answer:
Pad the image, expose kernel windows, flatten each window into a row, and multiply by flattened filters. Standard deep-learning conv2d is cross-correlation, so the kernel is not flipped. Output axes must be restored from (N,OH,OW,O) to NCHW. im2col is straightforward but can use substantial memory; the reference supports scalar stride and symmetric padding, not dilation or grouped convolution.

**Mathematical and practical explanation.** For kernel size $K$, padding $P$, and stride $s$, output height is $\lfloor(H+2P-K)/s\rfloor+1$, with the analogous width. The patch matrix has shape $(N H_{out}W_{out})\times(C_{in}K^2)$. Multiplying it by flattened filters produces every output location, which must then be reshaped with the correct axis order. [3](https://d2l.ai/)

For the implementation or system context discussed above, see [1](https://cs231n.github.io/convolutional-networks/) and [2](https://d2l.ai/chapter_convolutional-neural-networks/conv-layer.html).
